summary: Orphaned alert context and broken trace links after analytics partition reshard rollout
description: Issue summary: After a scheduled analytics partition reshard rollout (2026-03-10 03:00 UTC) a subset of console alerts for Northbound Health surface without any tracehook links or trace context. Impact: Customers receive alerts with 'Open trace' buttons that 404 or point to a placeholder; drilldowns from the dashboard do not include trace IDs. This affects alert triage and incident response for a subset of traces generated between the reshard window and the reindex.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) In prod (us-east), view alert group for rule 'LLM inference error rate > 2% (5m)'.
2) Click 'Open trace' from the alert details for alerts fired between 2026-03-10T03:00:00Z and 2026-03-10T03:45:00Z.
3) Observe 404 or trace search returning 'no trace found'.
4) Query raw ingestion events for tracehook_id present in alert payload and compare to indexed trace documents; some are missing or assigned to a different partition key.
logs:
[2026-03-10T03:02:11Z] ingest-partition-manager INFO started reshard job run_id=rs-20260310-01
[2026-03-10T03:07:44Z] event-writer WARN write-latency spike route=console/alerts partition=44 assigned_to=shard-7
[2026-03-10T03:08:10Z] trace-indexer ERROR doc-assign-mismatch tracehook_id=th_9f7a3 message=target-partition != event-partition
[2026-03-10T03:12:02Z] reindex-worker INFO enqueued doc_count=12k job_id=reindex-20260310-01
[2026-03-10T03:41:26Z] alerting-service INFO alert-fired id=AL-76543 tracehook_id=th_9f7a3 trace_link_status=missing
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: The reshard job updated routing metadata but did not immediately backfill new index keys for in-flight tracehook events, causing alert documents to link to non-existent trace index keys.
What we checked:
- Ingest and partition-manager logs around reshard window (see logs).
- Index mapping snapshots for trace-index before and after reshard.
- Alert documents in the alerts topic: some alerts refer to tracehook_id values that exist in raw events but were not present in trace-index due to temporary write routing to old shard.
Partial findings: The reshard operation applied new partition ranges but a delayed reindex task failed briefly (HTTP 502 from storage node) and retried leading to a window where alerting wrote references to traces that were not yet available in the consolidated index.
Risks: Until reindex completes, customers will see missing trace links and some dashboard drilldowns will be orphaned. This can reduce incident response efficiency and may violate response SLAs for enterprise customers.

2026-03-10 09:01 - Diego Moreno (SRE): Confirmed reshard job ran 03:00 UTC. Noted reindex-worker returned intermittent 502s between 03:10-03:15. Kicked-off ad-hoc reindex for affected partitions.
2026-03-10 10:34 - Support (Aisha): Shared workaround to customer: rerun alert drilldown after 30 minutes or use raw events export. Customer reported this is disruptive to on-call flow.

2026-03-11 02:22 - Ingrid Zhao (Observability Eng): Posted query that matches orphaned alerts and counts ~1.2k affected alert documents. Linked PR to modify reshard runbook: https://github.com/redwood/ops/pull/148

2026-03-12 07:05 - Diego Moreno (SRE): Reindex job completed for targeted partitions. Re-ran alert-to-trace reconciliation; ~98% of previously orphaned alerts now resolve to traces. Remaining ~2% appear to have been lost due to transient storage write errors and will require manual reconciliation.
resolution_summary: In-progress: A targeted reindex job was executed and reconciled ~98% of orphaned alert links. Short-term mitigation provided to customer (wait for reindex or use raw export). Root cause: reshard rollout + transient reindex-worker failures produced a time window where alerting wrote references to traces that had not been indexed. Permanent fix plan includes safer cutover sequencing and additional verification; see next_steps.
next_steps: 1) Update reshard runbook to include pausing alert write-paths or buffering alerts during partition cutover (owner: Ingrid Zhao, ETA: 2026-03-18).
2) Implement a pre-check in partition-manager to detect storage node 5xx rates and abort cutover if above threshold (owner: Diego Moreno, ETA: 2026-04-01).
3) Create a reconciliation tool to auto-link alerts to traces when index backfills complete; schedule as a follow-up PR (owner: Observability Team, ETA: 2026-03-25).
4) Postmortem to be published after remaining reconciliation work is done; include incident timeline and customer impact assessment.
